These aren't really useful for CodeEdit by itself to be exposed and don't allow anything that can't already be done with the gutter draw callback.
`_breakpoint_toggled` is triggered every time a breakpoint moves, both on the line it was at and the line it is at, so this method shouldn't be necessary.

It makes sense but this means the icons can't be accessed by `CodeEdit`. In this case, `ScriptTextEditor` will have to reimplement the gutter drawing callback so `CodeEdit`'s gutter will have different versions for the editor and runtime to maintain. Is this fine?

It's not the same. Toggling erases the breakpoint in the old line and adds a new breakpoint to the new line, the configuration is lost. I have to move the metadata when the lines move so I can't just toggle them like before.

Hmm. I think having it also in ScriptTextEditor would be better than exposing these icons and needing to preserve this drawing behavior for compatibility.
I think we could use a callback to override just the breakpoint drawing part of it.

The signals are sent from `CodeEdit::_text_changed` when the lines are moved, and the metadata is moved as well.
It looks like this method is just clearing all of them and setting them all again, so I don't see how it preserves anything compared to `_breakpoint_toggled`. Also `_breakpoint_toggled `is still being called for each moved breakpoint already, so if it caused anything to be lost it would still be happening.

It's more complex than this. `CodeEdit` can manage the metadata internally, but just the toggle signal doesn't work for an outside system like the debugger since there is more data than "breakpointed" or not to consider now. Breakpoints will be incorrect on the debugger side after lines move. I also had to consider not adding more signals and maintaining the previous behavior, which includes emitting `breakpoint_toggled` (there is even a test for this) although it doesn't work for this situation.. so I just clear the breakpoints which are invalid after the text change and set them again in the debugger.

Oh I see, the signal doesn't get emitted when there are breakpoints with different metadata next to each other.

There is still some duplicated work since the signal still emits when moved, but we can't really change the signal.
Maybe instead we can have a guard in `ScriptTextEditor::_breakpoint_toggled` that so it only sets the breakpoint if it was actually toggled? If not, then its fine.

I can register only a single callback, so I can't override just the breakpoint drawing. I would need to make helper methods public in `CodeEdit` just for this callback, but these reviews have all been about avoiding exposing things.

I moved the gutter drawing to ScriptTextEditor, which helps with the other review case too.

Since I moved the gutter drawing out of `CodeEdit`, there is no reason left for it to handle the breakpoint metadata internally.
